title: Suspicious PowerShell Network Activity
description: Scope outbound PowerShell connections on monitored devices and correlate them with published behavior and local incident evidence.
hypothesis: PowerShell used to retrieve a payload may leave a process-attributed network event.
considerations: Filter known administrative scripts and managed automation.
Review the full command line and initiating process ancestry.
Correlate destinations with internal DNS, proxy logs and approved intelligence.
Review the surrounding device timeline before broadening the lookback.

title: GSocket Process Activity
description: Find GSocket tooling in Linux endpoint process telemetry for review.
hypothesis: Known GSocket executable names or command-line references may identify investigated relay tooling.
considerations: Review the parent process, account and working path.
Confirm whether the activity was approved. GSocket is dual-use.
Review network events separately. Process execution alone cannot establish a relay session.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Phishing Destinations
description: Review network or proxy events for the exact downstream domains Microsoft reported.
hypothesis: Exact destination host matches can identify traffic associated with the documented phishing campaign.
considerations: Correlate matches with mail delivery and user click telemetry.
Use the action field to distinguish blocks from permitted requests.
Review URL paths and Entra sign-ins before inferring credential exposure.
Security scanners and automated previews can generate matches.

title: Quick Assist Process Activity
description: Find Quick Assist executions for triage alongside help desk records.
hypothesis: Fraudulent remote support sessions can start with Quick Assist process activity.
considerations: Check for an authorized support ticket and verify who initiated the session.
Review nearby process and network events for activity after the support session.
A process match cannot establish that a session connected.

title: Service Principal Sign-ins From a Reported IP
description: Review successful Entra service-principal sign-ins from a campaign-associated IP Microsoft reported.
hypothesis: A successful sign-in from the published address warrants correlation with app ownership and expected egress.
considerations: Review the service principal, credential changes and resource access.
Compare the source IP with known egress and require independent evidence before escalation.
Check Azure activity and resource audit logs for follow-on actions.
